Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Blockchain Architecture Design and Use Cases [NPT_4128]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Evaluate the modular architecture of Hyperledger Fabric 2.x, highlighting how endorsement,               (3)  
  validation, and commitment phases ensure transaction consistency.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)           Identify the function of Certificate Authority (CA) in Fabric and explain how it integrates with the     (3)  
  MSP for decentralized identity verification.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Distinguish Fabric's ordering mechanisms (Solo, Kafka, Raft) in terms of fault tolerance, scalability,   (4)  
  and use cases.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                Examine the steps of defining assets, participants, and transactions in Hyperledger Composer.            (3)  
  
  
  A)                                                           Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Defend the process of connecting a Composer Business Network to Fabric through REST API                  (3)  
  integration.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  C)           Design a blockchain-based patient-record management system using Composer and discuss its                (4)  
  security features.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
3)                Analyze the transformation in cross-border remittance systems enabled by blockchain.                     (3)  
  
  
  A)                                                           Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Relate the role of stablecoins and tokenization in enhancing financial transparency.                     (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Inspect the impact of blockchain on compliance and anti-money laundering (AML) practices.                (4)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

4)                       Defend blockchain provenance and explain its role in supply-chain traceability.                       (3)  
  
  
  A)                                                             Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)               Identify how IoT integration improves data authenticity in blockchain-based logistics networks.       (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)               Analyze IBM Food Trust as a case study of blockchain for food safety and consumer trust.              (4)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                       With a neat diagram, Appraise the end-to-end flow of deploying and invoking a smart contract in       (4)  
  Ethereum, including gas usage and state updates.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)               Utilize Proof-of-Stake mechanism and contrast it with Proof-of-Work in terms of efficiency and        (3)  
  security  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)               Examine a Merkle Tree. Explain its role in blockchain transaction verification with an example.       (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
